description:
Desktop AI agent with plugins, an embedded browser, workspace files, and local model support.

Lexora is a personal AI agent that evolves through hands-on work on your desktop. Beyond coding, it helps you organize research, refine creative projects, and plan everyday activities. Tell it what you want to accomplish, and it keeps working toward that goal, making words the starting point for work, creativity, and everyday life.
I started drafting this back in late September, worked on it on and off for over a month, and pushed hard over the past two weeks. Mobile remote control for your desktop tasks is finally here! For now, only Android is supported (if there’s strong interest from iOS users, please let me know—I’ll prioritize it faster based on your feedback).
🛠️ Task execution runs separately from the desktop interface
The desktop interface and task execution now run separately. Lexora Core runs in the background on your computer, and both desktop and Android connect to it. The desktop app opens faster, and you can keep the service running when you quit so your tasks can continue.
📱 Manage tasks remotely from Android
Start tasks, check progress, or add instructions to a running task from your phone. Tap an approval or question notification to open the relevant task and respond.
On desktop, enable connections in Settings → Mobile devices, then scan the pairing code with the Android app. Connect over your local network or Tailscale. Tasks still run on your computer, so it needs to be reachable and the Lexora background service needs to stay running.
